title: budget.v1
description: A file `budgets/<name>.yaml`: the impact one incident window may cause. It never says how an incident is made. Every class or key it does not name allows 0. `dialog_request_failed`, `call_cut`, `call_stranded`, `protocol_anomaly`, an `unexpected_ending` after answer (but a consult's contract refusal, below) and `unattributed` take no budget, so this schema has no place for them. ADR-0049.

name.description: Equal to the file stem; unique on the search path.

setup_failed.description: Allowances for failed setups. A failed setup matching no entry is a finding.

unexpected_ending.description: Allowances for pre-answer endings the catalog does not expect for a shape that does not expect an answer either (a reject with another code). After answer an unexpected ending takes no budget, with one exception: a catalog leg that opens only after an in-dialog consult (`after_consult`), left unopened while its asking leg received the consult's contract refusal on a call with no other failure, is allowed by code 0 and reason `leg:<role>`. The codes here are never 2xx.

setup_slow.description: Slow setups in the window. `threshold_ms` replaces the profile's `setup_slow_ms` inside the window; without an allowance, none may be slow.

over_outage.description: max_seconds counts beyond the window's outage, from its first inject to its last recovered.

cdr_mismatch.description: CDR mismatches in the window, by kind: `missing` (a call that owes a CDR has none), `extra` (a CDR no call of the run owns), `duplicate` (a second distinct CDR of a call), `differs` (a disposition or a duration other than the caller saw). A kind not named allows 0.

recovery.description: How traffic comes back after `healed`. Without `max_s`, it must be back before the window closes.

tolerance.description: The relative distance from the baseline that counts as back.

baseline_s.description: The length of the baseline, ending at `inject`.

hold_s.description: How long traffic must stay within tolerance to count as back.

latency_slack_ms.description: A span p99 is back within max(baseline × (1 + tolerance), baseline + latency_slack_ms): a relative tolerance alone is jitter on a setup of a few milliseconds.

limiter.description: What the window allows the profile's limiters (ADR-0049 §3.13), from its opening to its close plus the limiter's `repair_s`, each direction on its own: the median of admitted calls may reach every call the limiter's streams offer, cps × (ring + hold), with `overshoot: offered` (callers failing open admit them all; absent, the cap), and may fall under the steady band when `undershoot` is true (absent, never).

classes.description: Allowances for impact classes a product added on the search path (`classes/`), by class name. A built-in class name is refused here.

stream.description: A stream name, or `*` for each stream separately.

code.description: The final's status code; 0 for a setup that ended with no final (reason `timeout`, `transport` or `protocol`). Never a wildcard, never 2xx.

reason.description: The record's normalised `reason`, or `*` for any.

max_seconds.description: The allowance in seconds of the stream's offered rate: the count may reach max_seconds × the stream's cps in the window.

retry_after.description: Matches only a final that carried a Retry-After (true) or only one that carried none (false); absent, either. Tells a refusal that asks for a retry later from a bare one of the same code.

over_outage.description: max_seconds counts beyond the window's outage, from its first inject to its last recovered: the count may reach (max_seconds + outage) × the stream's cps, so one budget holds for any hold of the fault.

counted.description: One kind of a counted class: `max_calls`, or `max_seconds` of the summed offered rate of the run's `run` streams (calls end at the rate they start), optionally beyond the window's outage; for `differs`, `excess_ms` also allows every duration that differs from the caller's by at most that much past the join's own tolerance.

over_outage.description: max_seconds counts beyond the window's outage, from its first inject to its last recovered.
